artists.biography: Alex Kendall Somers is a Baltimore, Maryland based visual artist and musician who also lived for about 10 years in Reykjavík, Iceland with his longtime partner who is also a vocalist and guitar player for Icelandic post-rock band, Sigur Rós, Jón "Jónsi" Þór Birgisson. Upon their break-up, Somers resides in Los Angeles, California. He continues to release recordings and to work on film soundtracks and scores. Somers is also a raw food vegan and a founding member of Parachutes. He collaborated with Jónsi, producing visual art and music called Jónsi & Alex and released Riceboy Sleeps, their first instrumentals album. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Captain Fantastic (Music From The Film) is a film score composed by Alex Somers for the 2016 Matt Ross drama of the same name. Released in July 2016, the soundtrack comprises 24 instrumental tracks that accompany the film's narrative arc, ranging from brief atmospheric interludes to more developed compositional pieces. Somers employs a minimalist classical approach, utilizing piano, strings, and ambient textures to underscore the film's exploration of family dynamics and unconventional living.

The score demonstrates Somers' characteristic compositional style, blending orchestral elements with electronic and acoustic instrumentation to create an emotionally resonant soundscape. Tracks such as "Remembering" (7:16) and "Fortress" (4:37) showcase extended, contemplative passages, while shorter pieces like "A New Beginning" and "Home" function as transitional moments within the narrative. The music avoids melodramatic flourishes, instead favoring subtle harmonic progressions and textural development that complement rather than dominate the film's intimate scenes.

As a film score, Captain Fantastic represents a significant entry in Somers' body of work, establishing him as a composer capable of sustaining extended narrative structures through instrumental music. The album was released through Lakeshore Records in both digital and physical formats, reaching audiences interested in contemporary film music and classical composition. While the score received modest attention within soundtrack circles, it remains representative of the growing recognition of film scoring as a legitimate artistic medium within contemporary classical music.
